blocks.text: THE SITUATION — You are blamed in front of executives for a failure you did not create.
THE RESOURCEFUL RESPONSE — Do not spend the room proving your innocence emotionally. State the outcome, show the evidence, identify contributing factors, and propose the prevention step.

WORDS TO USE
“Here is what I can verify. Here is what I do not know yet. Here is the next action.”
THE SITUATION — A client says the service failed and threatens escalation.
THE RESOURCEFUL RESPONSE — Acknowledge impact, clarify the exact failure, avoid arguing about intent, state what you can fix now, and document the next commitment.

WORDS TO USE
“Here is what I can verify. Here is what I do not know yet. Here is the next action.”
THE SITUATION — A task is demanded by tomorrow although the normal process takes three days.
THE RESOURCEFUL RESPONSE — Ask what “done” means, separate must-have from nice-to-have, show the trade-off, and negotiate scope before silently accepting impossible work.

WORDS TO USE
“Here is what I can verify. Here is what I do not know yet. Here is the next action.”
THE SITUATION — You are handed a system you have never seen before.
THE RESOURCEFUL RESPONSE — Find the goal, inspect existing examples, search documentation, ask the person who knows it, and run the smallest safe test.

WORDS TO USE
“Here is what I can verify. Here is what I do not know yet. Here is the next action.”
THE SITUATION — You are in an unfamiliar city with weak connectivity.
THE RESOURCEFUL RESPONSE — Move toward a safe staffed location, use offline information, ask a trustworthy local institution for help, preserve battery, and keep identity documents secure.

WORDS TO USE
“Here is what I can verify. Here is what I do not know yet. Here is the next action.”
THE SITUATION — A message says your account will be closed unless you log in immediately.
THE RESOURCEFUL RESPONSE — Do not use the supplied link. Open the official service through a known route and verify the alert there.

WORDS TO USE
“Here is what I can verify. Here is what I do not know yet. Here is the next action.”
THE SITUATION — You want a raise but cannot prove the case.
THE RESOURCEFUL RESPONSE — Document outcomes, scope, responsibilities, market context where appropriate, and the next level you are prepared to handle; negotiate from evidence and alternatives.

WORDS TO USE
“Here is what I can verify. Here is what I do not know yet. Here is the next action.”
THE SITUATION — A conversation has become a contest to win.
THE RESOURCEFUL RESPONSE — Lower the tempo, identify the actual issue, state your boundary or need clearly, and stop trying to force agreement where only respectful disagreement is possible.

WORDS TO USE
“Here is what I can verify. Here is what I do not know yet. Here is the next action.”
THE SITUATION — The same error happens every week.
THE RESOURCEFUL RESPONSE — Map the process, inspect handoffs and incentives, find the earliest reliable control point, test a change, and document the new workflow.

WORDS TO USE
“Here is what I can verify. Here is what I do not know yet. Here is the next action.”
THE SITUATION — An AI assistant gives a fluent but suspicious answer.
THE RESOURCEFUL RESPONSE — Extract the claim, locate the underlying source, check the date, compare with another authority, and downgrade confidence until verified.

WORDS TO USE
“Here is what I can verify. Here is what I do not know yet. Here is the next action.”
